Photo showing the port paddlewheel support arm. Notice the unprotected sections on the right and left of the photo.
Physical barricades such as warning chains, bars, gates, and railings serve much the same function as
safety policies: They provide one more way to keep people from falling prey to their own lapses of
memory or judgment. A warning sign, however large and colored, does not provide any physical way to
restrict access to a dangerous area. Similarly, barricades such as the chains found hanging on the P/V
QUEEN OF THE WEST, which are not utilized to protect crew or passengers, are simply useless. Vessel
management must place barricades in effective areas of the vessel and then empower supervisors to hold
crew accountable for failure to place them in service.
3. Rescue effort: After Mr. Staples fell into the water, his subsequent rescue was unsuccessful.
Although the efforts of the crew to save him were highly commendable, a number of events transpired to
reduce the likelihood that he was rescued in time:
Lighted deck: An overhead light rests on the port side of the paddlewheel support arms about eight
feet up on the accommodation bulkhead. The three witnesses could not agree if it was on at the time
of the incident. The light is not part of the rest of the vessel's deck light system, and must be turned
on manually from an independent switch inside the garbage room. Some crew members stated that
they leave the light in the "off’ position when they go to the stern to smoke, because the added
illumination allows personnel supervisors to observe them smoking (in violation of company policy).
